name: Tanganyika (1923–1961)
description: A British Red Ensign — red with the Union Flag in the canton — charged in the fly with a white disc bearing the head of a giraffe.
history: Britain administered Tanganyika Territory, the bulk of the former German East Africa, under a League of Nations mandate from 1922 and later as a United Nations trust territory. As a mandate it had no national flag of its own — the Union Flag was official — but from 1923 this Red Ensign defaced with the territorial badge, a giraffe's head on a white disc, served as its ensign and is the flag conventionally shown for Tanganyika of the period; a Blue Ensign with the same badge was the government ensign. It gave way to the green-and-black national flag at independence on 9 December 1961. EAT is the alpha-3 code element indeterminately reserved for Tanganyika under the UN road-traffic conventions.

features.symbolism: British administration under the League of Nations mandate

features.role: white disc bearing the territorial badge
